title: The American Statistical Association's 2016 statement on p-values
summary: Wasserstein and Lazar published the ASA's warning about how p-values are used.
body: Ronald L. Wasserstein and Nicole A. Lazar, "The ASA Statement on p-Values: Context, Process, and Purpose" (The American Statistician, 2016), is the association's public statement. A p-value is not the probability that a hypothesis is true, and a threshold such as 0.05 is a convention. The statement exists because those misreadings were common. This card records the document. It does not retype the six principles from memory.
